recall.minute: TD(0) updates V(S) toward R + γV(S′) after every step (0.5 + 0.1 × 1.04 = 0.604), combining Monte Carlo's model-free sampling with DP's bootstrapping. Its target has lower variance than the MC return but is biased while V is wrong; it works online and in continuing tasks, and batch TD converges to the certainty-equivalence estimate, which helps on Markov tasks (faster than MC on the random walk). SARSA (on-policy) uses the next action actually taken: 0.5 + 0.5(1 + 0.63 − 0.5) = 1.065. Q-learning (off-policy) uses the max: 1.11, and converges to q* regardless of behaviour if all pairs are visited. Expected SARSA averages over π, lowering variance and generalising both. Maximisation bias makes max-based targets optimistic (in the A/B example Q-learning picks the worse 'left' action far too often); Double Q-learning selects with one table and evaluates with the other. On cliff walking SARSA takes the safe path and earns about −35 per episode while exploring; Q-learning learns the optimal edge path but earns about −49 because exploration sometimes drops it off the cliff.
